did_you_know.text: Did you know? King Darius ordered a search for Cyrus’s decree in the treasury archives in Babylon to verify the instructions concerning the construction in Jerusalem.
Did you know? Cyrus’s decree was found at Ecbatana, the citadel in the province of Media. It was written on a scroll and recorded the king’s decision.
Did you know? Cyrus’s decree specified that the temple of the Lord in Jerusalem was to be sixty cubits high and sixty cubits wide.
Did you know? According to Cyrus’s decree, the building was to have three courses of dressed stone and one course of new timber, with the costs paid from the royal treasury.
Did you know? Cyrus ordered that the gold and silver articles Nebuchadnezzar had taken from the temple be returned to Jerusalem and put back in their places in the temple.
Did you know? Darius ordered Tattenai and the officials of the province west of the Euphrates not to interfere with the work on the house of God, but to allow the Jews to build it on its site.
Did you know? Darius decreed that the construction costs were to be paid from the royal treasury, using the taxes collected in the province west of the Euphrates, so that the work would not stop.

Did you know? The decree required that the priests in Jerusalem be supplied daily with animals, grain, salt, wine, and oil for the sacrifices, so that they could pray for the well-being of the king and his sons.
Did you know? The temple was completed on the third day of the month of Adar, in the sixth year of the reign of King Darius.
Did you know? At the dedication of the temple, they sacrificed one hundred bulls, two hundred rams, four hundred lambs, and twelve male goats as a sin offering—one goat for each tribe of Israel.
